botDirectoryGroups.label: Surface and raid threats
botDirectoryGroups.title: Farm bots that attack crops, players, and creations
botDirectoryGroups.description: Use this group when the search means enemy farm bots rather than crafting stations. Color is not cosmetic: Totebot and Tapebot variants change movement, attack type, and target priority.

rows.name: Green Totebot
rows.response: Split the pack and avoid backing into crop rows.

rows.name: Haybot
rows.output: Scrap Metal plus a bonus roll
rows.response: Read the wind-up and fight in an open lane.

rows.name: Blue Totebot
rows.encounter: Water routes and land after provocation
rows.output: Independent chances for Circuit Board, Glue, and a rare Drill
rows.response: Leave the water before committing to close combat.

rows.name: Yellow Totebot
rows.behavior: Jumping stomp that crosses floors and ceilings
rows.response: Do not rely on a low roof as the only barrier.

rows.name: Red Explosive Totebot
rows.response: Make it the first target and keep it away from storage.

rows.name: Tapebot family
rows.behavior: Ranged tape, explosive tape, bubbles, or slowing ink
rows.response: Break line of sight; identify color before peeking.

rows.name: Farmbot
rows.behavior: Heavy melee, kick, and pesticide pressure
rows.response: Budget ammunition and keep it off the vehicle.

botDirectoryGroups.label: Drilling Thunder encounters
botDirectoryGroups.title: New bots tied to underground travel and story encounters
botDirectoryGroups.description: These bots solve very different combat problems. A general-purpose farm wall does not answer digging Cablebots, ceiling Minerbots, an invulnerable Scannerbot event, and a staged Trashbot boss fight in the same way.

rows.name: Cablebot
rows.behavior: Bites, jumps, attacks creations, and can dig
rows.response: Protect exposed working parts and clear it before repairs.

rows.name: Minerbot
rows.output: Component Kit and tier-matched ore nuggets
rows.response: Scan overhead space and leave room for the crash.

rows.name: Scannerbot
rows.behavior: Mobile missile platform; normal attacks do not damage it
rows.response: Use terrain and movement; treat survival as the objective.

rows.name: Drillbot
rows.output: Encounter progression rather than a farmable drop
rows.response: Read the phase objective instead of firing at every surface.

rows.name: Trashbot
rows.behavior: Two staged fights with pattern and weak-point windows
rows.response: Damage the open eye, then use the exposed core window.

botDirectoryGroups.label: Non-aggressive and resource carriers
botDirectoryGroups.title: Bots and creatures that should not be treated like raid enemies
botDirectoryGroups.description: Seedbot and Lootbot flee from nearby players and do not run attack states. Wocs and Glowbs are creatures, but players commonly include them in bot searches because they convert feed into useful farm resources.

rows.name: Seedbot
rows.behavior: Flees; carries one visible seed-crate type
rows.output: Matching seeds when damaged or destroyed
rows.response: Identify the crate before deciding whether to chase it.

rows.name: Lootbot
rows.behavior: Flees and releases one reward per accepted hit
rows.output: Materials, produce, fuel, Batteries, or special raid reward
rows.response: Keep the route clear and land deliberate hits.

rows.name: Woc
rows.response: Use a calm feeding pocket outside raid lanes.

rows.name: Glowb
rows.behavior: Passive creature that seeks Cardboard Blocks
rows.response: Feed on reachable ground and collect the Glow promptly.

botDirectoryGroups.label: Player-operated bot stations
botDirectoryGroups.title: Bots that craft, refine, cook, unlock, or process resources
botDirectoryGroups.description: These are placeable stations, not autonomous farm workers. They do not plant or harvest a field by themselves; the player supplies ingredients or connects containers and chooses a recipe.

rows.name: Craftbot
rows.output: Parts, blocks, machines, and unlocked rewards
rows.response: Use the Recipes directory to check ingredients and unlocks.

rows.name: Cookbot
rows.output: Pizza Burger, Veggie Burger, Revival Baguette
rows.response: Bring the exact crop quantities; it does not grow crops.

rows.name: Refinebot
rows.response: Pair it with a Resource Collector for a clean input path.

rows.name: Schematicbot
rows.output: Recipe access, not a finished item
rows.response: Match the scan method to the recipe you need.

rows.name: Crushbot / Prospectorbot / Sawbot
rows.output: Crushed ore, selected materials, and sawn outputs
rows.response: Plan the whole input-to-storage chain before placing machines.

botBuildRoutes.change: Create a repairable outer lane and keep moving parts behind the first impact line.

botBuildRoutes.change: Add hard line-of-sight breaks; a taller open fence does not stop ranged shots.

botQuestions.question: Are there neutral or friendly bots in Scrap Mechanic?
botQuestions.answer: Seedbots and Lootbots are non-aggressive resource carriers: both flee when a player gets close and neither runs a normal attack state. Wocs and Glowbs are passive creatures, while crafting bots are placeable stations.

botQuestions.question: Which Scrap Mechanic bot gives crop seeds?
botQuestions.answer: Seedbot carries one visible seed-crate type. The current set covers Tomato, Redbeet, Carrot, Potato, Cotton, Pigment Flower, Banana, Blueberry, Orange, Broccoli, Pineapple, and Chili. Damage can release matching seeds, and destroying the bot releases an additional matching bundle.

botQuestions.question: Does the Cookbot grow or harvest crops?
botQuestions.answer: No. Cookbot only consumes supplied ingredients for three food recipes. Planting, watering, and harvesting require the player or a creation using Vacuum Pumps and water-delivery parts.

botQuestions.question: What is the difference between a Farmbot and farming bots?
botQuestions.answer: Farmbot is the named red heavy enemy. Farming bots is a loose player phrase that may mean every hostile agricultural robot, the robots in a farm raid, or player-operated stations such as Craftbot and Cookbot.

botQuestions.question: Is the Seeker Bot the Scannerbot?
botQuestions.answer: Players often use Seeker Bot for the large roaming missile bot. The current game files name the unit Scannerbot. Normal projectile, melee, explosion, and collision callbacks do not reduce it, so use cover and movement rather than treating it as a normal health-bar fight.

botQuestions.question: Which bots can appear when crops trigger a raid?
botQuestions.answer: The answer depends on crop value, crop count, raid tier, night, and the current 1.0 raid configuration. Use the Raid Calculator for the current wave instead of relying on an old fixed list.
